finding.description: Describes a defect in the same-role review, not a candidate defect already captured by a supported review finding.

reviewFindingAdjudication.description: Judges one finding made by the same-role review rather than judging the candidate defect again.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain why this review finding is rejected; this array is empty when judgment is supported.

surfaceAdjudication.description: Echoes the bound same-role review assessment in reviewAssessmentJudgment and judges the soundness of that assessment in judgment. A sound blocking review assessment is blocking plus supported, not an adjudication failure.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain a rejected same-role review assessment. It is empty for supported; rejected requires a linked blocking finding on this surface.

judgment.description: supported approves the same-role review assessment even when reviewAssessmentJudgment is blocking; rejected means the assessment is unsound or incomplete.

reviewAssessmentJudgment.description: Exact echo of the bound same-role review assessment's judgment; the deterministic verifier rejects any mismatch.

adjudicationSchema.description: This record judges the soundness and completeness of the same-role review, not the candidate.

findings.description: Adjudicator findings describe defects in the same-role review's requirement, assessment, reasoning, finding, coverage, or severity; they do not repeat candidate defects already captured by supported review findings.

reviewFindingAdjudications.description: Each entry judges one same-role review finding. A supported review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected review finding requires a linked blocking adjudicator finding that explains the review defect.

surfaceAdjudications.description: Each entry exactly echoes the same-role review assessment's pass, advisory, or blocking judgment, then separately judges that assessment as supported or rejected; it does not judge the candidate surface directly.

verdict.description: pass means the same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate; fail means the same-role review is unsound or incomplete. This verdict never judges the candidate directly.

adjudicationSchema.title: Independent canonical-English semantic adjudication record

adjudicationSemantics.failMeaning: The same-role review is unsound or incomplete.
adjudicationSemantics.findingLinkMeaning: A supported surface assessment or review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected one links at least one blocking adjudicator finding on an overlapping surface that explains a defect in the review.
adjudicationSemantics.passMeaning: The same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate.
adjudicationSemantics.subject: same-role-review
adjudicationSemantics.surfaceAdjudicationMeaning: Each surface adjudication exactly echoes the bound review assessment judgment in reviewAssessmentJudgment, then uses judgment supported or rejected to judge that assessment.

findings.correctionCriterion: Within each frozen practice or answer unit, identify the requested or reported variance, standard deviation, and uniform bound, and retain the applicable fan-in and fan-out values locally.
findings.evidence: Unit.038 asks to recalculate 'the three quantities' without naming them. Unit.047 lists the three results but does not state the fan-in 2/fan-out 2 condition required for that checked result. Unit.048 begins 'They become' and gives three unlabeled numbers without either the quantity names or the fan-in 4/fan-out 2 condition.
findings.learnerConsequence: The isolated task cannot identify what to calculate, and the isolated checked results cannot reliably map their numbers to the requested quantities and width conditions.

findings.correctionCriterion: Identify the two columns as input-weight gradient columns and state the zero-SiLU evaluation condition and equal downstream treatment locally enough to scope the derivative and equality explanation.
findings.evidence: Unit.049 says 'Both columns are [0.5,-0.5]^\top' without identifying the columns as input-weight gradients, and says 'SiLU contributes derivative 1/2' without stating the zero-input evaluation condition. The frozen unit does not name the zero-weight graph.
findings.learnerConsequence: A reader cannot identify the reported matrix columns from this answer alone and may understand the stated SiLU derivative as unconditional rather than evaluated at zero.

findings.correctionCriterion: State within both units that the depth-table values are expected signal variances computed from target weight variances under the independent-linear model, rather than measured propagation of the sampled matrices.
findings.evidence: Units.066 and .067 explicitly call the histogram spread 'measured', but describe the other evidence only as 'A separate independent-linear depth table' and say that Xavier weights 'keep it unchanged'. Neither unit identifies those depth values as expected or computed from target distribution variances.
findings.learnerConsequence: The standalone caption and nonvisual description leave open whether the displayed variance preservation was measured for the sampled matrices, despite their frozen requirement to distinguish measured distributions from theoretical propagation.

findings.correctionCriterion: Identify the reference bound that is doubled in the standalone card's starting-rule label.
findings.evidence: Unit.073 labels the rule 'Uniform weights: doubled bound' and gives its numeric bound and measured statistics, but does not name the bound relative to which it is doubled.
findings.learnerConsequence: The numeric interval remains interpretable, but the standalone comparison label does not identify its comparison baseline.

findings.correctionCriterion: Identify the compared original-seed matrix and the unchanged-request scope locally; in the checked answer, make clear that the observed difference is between resulting tensor values, not merely between requests with different seeds.
findings.evidence: Unit.051 says 'The selected seed-18 request differs in this example', which names a request difference rather than the resulting tensor difference and supplies no comparison baseline. Unit.077 names seed 18 but refers only to 'the original-seed matrix', without identifying that original seed or stating which request remains fixed.
findings.learnerConsequence: The isolated results do not specify the reproducibility comparison precisely, and the checked answer can be read as the trivial fact that the seed-18 request itself differs rather than evidence about generated weights.
